text: can you explain gradint decend in 3d surface

Given: Error surface: z=f(x,y)=x^2+y^2., Initial point: (x_0,y_0)=(3,2), so the starting surface point is (3,2,13)., Learning rate: \eta=0.2., Update rule: (x_{k+1},y_{k+1})=(x_k,y_k)-\eta\nabla f(x_k,y_k).
Find: The successive positions of the moving point and the limiting minimum approached by gradient descent.

1. Define the three-dimensional error surface
   z=f(x,y)=x²+y²
   The height z represents the error. For every horizontal position (x,y), the surface height is x^2+y^2. Because squares are nonnegative, the surface is a bowl-shaped paraboloid.

2. Identify the minimum
   f(0,0)=0²+0²=0
   Both x^2 and y^2 are nonnegative, so their sum cannot be less than zero. The smallest possible error is therefore z=0, reached at (x,y)=(0,0). The corresponding point on the 3D surface is (0,0,0).

3. Compute the gradient
   ∇ f(x,y)=begin bmatrix(∂ f)/(∂ x)\\[2pt](∂ f)/(∂ y)end bmatrix=begin bmatrix2x\\2yend bmatrix
   The verified partial derivatives form the gradient vector. At each horizontal location, the gradient points in the direction in which the surface height increases most rapidly.

4. Explain why the negative gradient moves downhill
   -∇ f(x,y)=begin bmatrix-2x\\-2yend bmatrix
   The gradient points away from the origin, toward larger values of x^2+y^2. Reversing it points toward the origin, where the bowl is lower. Thus subtracting the gradient moves the point downhill on the surface.

5. Write the gradient-descent update
   begin alignedxₖ₊₁&=xₖ-η(2xₖ),\y ₖ₊₁&=yₖ-η(2yₖ).end aligned
   Substitute the gradient from Step 3 into the gradient-descent rule. One update changes both horizontal coordinates; the new surface height is then evaluated at the new coordinates.

6. Substitute the selected learning rate
   begin alignedxₖ₊₁&=xₖ-0.2(2xₖ)=0.6xₖ,\y ₖ₊₁&=yₖ-0.2(2yₖ)=0.6yₖ.end aligned
   Using \eta=0.2 makes each coordinate 60% of its previous value. Since the magnitude is multiplied by 0.6, the point moves closer to the origin at every step without alternating across it.

7. Perform the first update from the concrete starting point
   begin aligned(x₁,y₁)&=(0.6x₀,0.6y₀)\\&=(0.6·3,0.6·2)\\&=(1.8,1.2),\z ₁&=1.8²+1.2²=4.68.end aligned
   The point begins at (3,2,13) and moves to (1.8,1.2,4.68). The surface height has decreased from 13 to 4.68, demonstrating one downhill step.

8. Show several successive positions
   begin arrayc|c|c|ck&xₖ&yₖ&zₖ=xₖ²+yₖ²\\hline 0&3&2&13\\1&1.8&1.2&4.68\\2&1.08&0.72&1.6848\\3&0.648&0.432&0.605…\\4&0.3888&0.2592&0.2178…\\5&0.23328&0.15552&0.0784…end array
   The computed trajectory shows the moving point descending the bowl. Both horizontal coordinates and the error z become smaller at each displayed step, so an animation can plot these points in order and connect them with a descending path.

9. Verify the decrease and convergence factor
   zₖ₊₁=(0.6xₖ)²+(0.6yₖ)²=0.36(xₖ²+yₖ²)=0.36zₖ
   The verified identity shows that each iteration multiplies the error by 0.36. Because 0.36 is between 0 and 1, the error decreases geometrically and approaches zero. The coordinates likewise approach the origin.

10. State the limiting result for the moving point
   boxed (xₖ,yₖ)longrightarrow (0,0), zₖ=xₖ²+yₖ²longrightarrow 0
   Starting from (3,2) and using the fixed learning rate 0.2, gradient descent approaches the minimum at (0,0,0). The point does not need to reach the minimum in finitely many steps; it gets progressively closer as the iterations continue.

Answer: boxed begin aligned∇ f(x,y)&=(2x,2y),\\(xₖ₊₁,yₖ₊₁)&=(xₖ,yₖ)-0.2(2xₖ,2yₖ)\\&=(0.6xₖ,0.6yₖ),\\(x₀,y₀)=(3,2)&Longrightarrow (xₖ,yₖ)→(0,0),\z ₖ&=xₖ²+yₖ²→0.end aligned
For the bowl z=x^2+y^2, the gradient is (2x,2y), which points uphill away from the origin. Gradient descent subtracts this vector. With learning rate 0.2, each step changes (x_k,y_k) to (0.6x_k,0.6y_k). Starting from (3,2), the point follows (1.8,1.2), (1.08,0.72), (0.648,0.432), and so on. The error is multiplied by 0.36 at each step, so the point approaches the minimum (0,0,0) without oscillating.

operations.title: The Error Surface
operations.caption: z=f(x,y)=x^2+y^2
operations.narration: Imagine error as height. At every horizontal location x and y, the bowl assigns the height z equal to x squared plus y squared.

operations.title: The Minimum
operations.caption: f(0,0)=0^2+0^2=0
operations.narration: Squares cannot be negative, so their sum cannot be below zero. The bowl reaches its minimum at the origin, where the surface point is zero, zero, zero.

operations.title: The Uphill Direction
operations.caption: \nabla f(x,y)=\begin{bmatrix}2x\\2y\end{bmatrix}
operations.narration: The gradient collects the two partial derivatives. It points in the horizontal direction where the surface rises most rapidly, away from the origin on this bowl.

operations.title: Reverse the Arrow
operations.caption: -\nabla f(x,y)=\begin{bmatrix}-2x\\-2y\end{bmatrix}
operations.narration: The gradient points uphill. Reversing it gives the negative gradient, which points toward the lower part of the bowl. This is the direction gradient descent follows.

operations.title: The Update Rule
operations.caption: \begin{aligned}x_{k+1}&=x_k-\eta(2x_k),\\y_{k+1}&=y_k-\eta(2y_k).\end{aligned}
operations.narration: At each step, keep the current point, subtract a scaled gradient, and use the result as the next horizontal position. The learning rate eta controls the step size.

operations.title: Choose the Step Size
operations.caption: \begin{aligned}x_{k+1}&=x_k-0.2(2x_k)=0.6x_k,\\y_{k+1}&=y_k-0.2(2y_k)=0.6y_k.\end{aligned}
operations.narration: With learning rate zero point two, each coordinate is multiplied by zero point six. The point moves closer to the origin without oscillating across it.

operations.title: The First Step
operations.caption: (x_1,y_1)=(1.8,1.2),\qquad z_1=4.68
operations.narration: Start at horizontal coordinates three, two, where the error is thirteen. Multiplying both coordinates by zero point six moves the point to one point eight, one point two, where the error is four point six eight.

operations.title: A Descending Trajectory
operations.caption: z_k=x_k^2+y_k^2
operations.narration: Repeat the same update. The coordinates and the error shrink at every displayed step as the point heads toward the center.

operations.title: Why the Error Shrinks
operations.caption: z_{k+1}=0.36z_k
operations.narration: Both coordinates are multiplied by zero point six, so their squares are multiplied by zero point three six. Therefore the error is multiplied by zero point three six at every step and approaches zero.

operations.title: Final Result
operations.caption: \boxed{(x_k,y_k)\longrightarrow(0,0),\qquad z_k=x_k^2+y_k^2\longrightarrow0}
operations.narration: Starting from three, two with learning rate zero point two, the iterates approach the minimum at zero, zero, zero, and the error approaches zero because each coordinate is multiplied by zero point six.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class GeneratedScene(ThreeDScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_camera_orientation(phi=65 * DEGREES, theta=-55 * DEGREES, zoom=0.82)

        axes = ThreeDAxes(
            x_range=[-0.5, 3.5, 1],
            y_range=[-0.5, 2.5, 1],
            z_range=[0, 14, 2],
            x_length=5.4,
            y_length=4.6,
            z_length=4.8,
        )
        axis_labels = axes.get_axis_labels(
            x_label=MathTex("x", font_size=40),
            y_label=MathTex("y", font_size=40),
            z_label=MathTex("z", font_size=40),
        )

        bowl = Surface(
            lambda u, v: axes.c2p(u, v, u**2 + v**2),
            u_range=[-0.05, 3.15],
            v_range=[-0.05, 2.15],
            resolution=(24, 20),
            fill_opacity=0.62,
            checkerboard_colors=[BLUE_D, BLUE_E],
            stroke_color=BLUE_B,
            stroke_width=0.5,
        )

        title = MathTex(r"z=x^2+y^2", font_size=38, color=BLUE_C)
        rule = MathTex(
            r"(x,y)\leftarrow(x,y)-\eta\nabla f(x,y)",
            font_size=28,
        )
        eta = MathTex(r"\eta=0.2", font_size=32, color=YELLOW)
        direction = MathTex(
            r"-\nabla f\;\text{points downhill}",
            font_size=25,
            color=GREEN_C,
        )
        panel = VGroup(title, rule, eta, direction).arrange(
            DOWN,
            aligned_edge=LEFT,
            buff=0.28,
        )
        panel.to_corner(UR, buff=0.45)
        self.add_fixed_in_frame_mobjects(panel)

        values = [
            np.array([3.0, 2.0, 13.0]),
            np.array([1.8, 1.2, 4.68]),
            np.array([1.08, 0.72, 1.6848]),
            np.array([0.648, 0.432, 0.606528]),
            np.array([0.3888, 0.2592, 0.21835008]),
            np.array([0.0, 0.0, 0.0]),
        ]
        scene_values = [axes.c2p(*point) for point in values]

        start_dot = Dot3D(scene_values[0], radius=0.12, color=YELLOW)
        start_label = MathTex(r"(3,2,13)", font_size=32, color=YELLOW)
        start_label.move_to(axes.c2p(2.45, 2.15, 13.5))

        min_dot = Dot3D(scene_values[-1], radius=0.1, color=RED)
        min_label = MathTex(r"\min=(0,0,0)", font_size=32, color=RED)
        min_label.move_to(axes.c2p(0.3, 0.35, 0.8))

        segments = [
            Line3D(
                scene_values[i],
                scene_values[i + 1],
                thickness=0.035,
                color=YELLOW,
            )
            for i in range(5)
        ]
        arrows = [
            Arrow3D(
                scene_values[i],
                scene_values[i + 1],
                color=GREEN_C,
                thickness=0.035,
                height=0.18,
                base_radius=0.055,
            )
            for i in range(5)
        ]

        moving_dot = Dot3D(scene_values[0], radius=0.14, color=ORANGE)
        iter_label = MathTex(r"k=0", font_size=32, color=ORANGE)
        iter_label.move_to(axes.c2p(2.25, 0.2, 11.2))

        self.play(
            Create(axes),
            Create(axis_labels),
            FadeIn(bowl),
            FadeIn(panel),
            run_time=2.2,
        )
        self.wait(0.8)

        self.play(
            FadeIn(start_dot),
            FadeIn(start_label),
            FadeIn(min_dot),
            FadeIn(min_label),
            FadeIn(moving_dot),
            FadeIn(iter_label),
            run_time=1.2,
        )
        self.wait(0.7)

        self.play(
            Create(segments[0]),
            Create(arrows[0]),
            moving_dot.animate.move_to(scene_values[1]),
            Transform(
                iter_label,
                MathTex(r"k=1", font_size=32, color=ORANGE).move_to(
                    iter_label.get_center()
                ),
            ),
            run_time=1.8,
        )

        self.play(
            Create(segments[1]),
            Create(arrows[1]),
            moving_dot.animate.move_to(scene_values[2]),
            Transform(
                iter_label,
                MathTex(r"k=2", font_size=32, color=ORANGE).move_to(
                    iter_label.get_center()
                ),
            ),
            run_time=1.5,
        )

        self.play(
            Create(VGroup(*segments[2:])),
            Create(VGroup(*arrows[2:])),
            Succession(
                *[
                    moving_dot.animate.move_to(scene_values[i])
                    for i in range(3, 6)
                ],
                lag_ratio=0.05,
            ),
            Transform(
                iter_label,
                MathTex(r"k\to\infty", font_size=32, color=ORANGE).move_to(
                    iter_label.get_center()
                ),
            ),
            run_time=2.8,
        )
        self.wait(0.9)
